- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and news volume drops, model overreacts to recent highs; adjust downward by 1–4% for 5–10 day horizon.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–30 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment average <0.5.
- If sentiment change is sharply negative (e.g., -1.00) followed by a spike, model may lag; forecast should be adjusted upward 1–3% in next 2–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates true volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is volatile or news volume >2.0.
